title: Level 2 (Intermediate) - A-6
notes:
West leads a trump against 4♥, which South wins in hand. South must lose a trick to the ♠A and the ♣A. South thus must find a way to dispose of one of his 2 diamond losers.

If West holds the ♦K, a simple finesse in that suit will solve South's problems. If that finesse loses, South will be in trouble. The defense will continue hearts, drawing another of North's trumps. A diamond is now played to North's ♦A with the hope of ruffing South's remaining diamond loser.

Now declarer must lead either a spade or a club from the dummy. The defense will take the ♠A or ♣A and lead a third round of hearts exhausting North's trumps and leaving South with a certain diamond loser.

South can give himself a much better chance by simply cashing the ♦A and playing the ♦Q, conceding a trick to the ♦K. As the diamond suit is now unblocked, South can win the trump continuation and ruff his last diamond in the dummy. South concedes the ♠A and ♣A, drawing the last trump as soon as he can.
